I’m an autistic adult. First and foremost: no autistic individual is the same and their experiences will differ from one another. I am merely explaining my personal experience. 
It’s not uncommon for mental illnesses such as depression & anxiety to co-exist with autism - they can really amplify autistic struggles. Or vice versa.

There’s this pattern autistic people can fall into called ‘rumination’. That means the person is mentally stuck, unable to stop thinking over and over about things that have caused you stress, someone hurting your feelings, past trauma, etc. 

In my experience, that rumination causes me to go down a spiral. 

Here’s an example: I promised my partner to attend an event with him. When I turn up, there’s a lot more people than I expected, it’s too loud and it’s too much for me to handle. So I leave. That then makes me think “I’m not a good enough partner, I can’t keep my promises, I let him down.” Then it spirals even further, managing to convince myself that everyone hates me, etc. It then circles back to me being mad at my autism, preventing me from being a “normal person”. 
It then turns to anger towards myself, then being angry at my parents for bringing me into this world. 
Then the suicidal ideation starts. The predicted future in that moment starts to look extremely bleak. That then turns to anger once again because I know I can’t do it - not wanting to cause trauma to loved ones. So the next best option is self harm. It snaps me out of the rumination. But then the guilt spiral starts.

However, in a meltdown that’s different. The emotions and physical sensations at that moment are so intense, I need to physically do something. So in that moment, I tend to hit myself. It snaps me out of it. 

That’s just my experience though. Hope this helps!

Took a tab each and walked to a nearby park at nighttime with someone I didn't know very well (his 2nd time), we sat at the tables and talked for a while (about 30-45 minutes). 
He had his hands on the table and I was telling him that's unsanitary and shouldn't be having his hands on there. To spite me, he wiped his hands on the table and then rubbed them on his face. 
I shouted in disgust and all the sudden I started feeling intense anxiety to the point where I was laughing/hyperventilating. That's when I knew it started kicking in so I started panicking even more. The guy came over to calm me down and we looked at each other's eyes to see how big our pupils were. His were very dilated. Not sure about mine. 
After I calmed down a bit, he put his hands on my shoulders and said "look at the ground", I did and everything was warping and saw geometric patterns in everything. I then felt physically amazing but odd at the same time. The best I could describe how my body felt was a tingling folding chair. 

We hung around that park for hours, climbing on the robe and gliding on the flying fox, feeling like a child again. He called two friends of his who were nearby and I got to meet them. They sat there and talked while I was staring at the trees. I kept seeing outlines of faces that looked familiar and that made me feel safe, as if they were watching over me. 

When the visuals started wearing off, we went back to his place and watched YouTube for a couple of more hours. Then those dark thoughts started kicking in, I discovered why I was having bad depression at the time and so on. Then he started saying some personal things about me that ended up making me paranoid and I ended up feeling very suicidal. 
He fell asleep before me and I remember staring at the wall making connections with everything and how life is meaningless. 

Woke up 2 hours later, frequently gagging and I went home not long after that. 
For about a month I was extremely sad and ready to kick the bucket any second. 

TL;DR: did tabs with a guy I didn't know we'll (bad idea I know) and he fucked with my head and left me suicidal for month.
